findings.title: Scheduled report timestamps render in UTC instead of workspace (Pacific) timezone
findings.description: Cedar Grove Schools' scheduled/emailed PDF reports show timestamps roughly seven hours ahead of their Pacific workspace time, causing sessions to appear as if they happened at midnight. The issue has been occurring for at least a month. The live in-app dashboard shows correct times; only the scheduled/emailed report output is affected. Directors use the report to compare session activity against the school day, so the incorrect timestamps led them to question the accuracy of the underlying data.
findings.quote: Looks like about seven hours ahead of us. We're Pacific. A report that should say 9am shows up stamped around 4pm.
findings.severity_reason: Incorrect timestamps are feeding into district directors' decisions about workday vs after-hours engagement, undermining trust in the data even though the underlying data is correct.
findings.match_note: Same symptom (scheduled/emailed report timestamps shown in UTC vs workspace timezone) and same consistent ~7hr offset as PROJ-101; customer explicitly confirms in-app view is unaffected, matching PROJ-101's scope description.

findings.title: Login page stock photo ('Salad Susan') seen as corny by teachers
findings.description: Will mentions the login page's stock photo of a woman laughing with a laptop near a salad is considered corny by teachers, who jokingly call her 'Salad Susan.' He explicitly frames this as a running joke, not a request, and directly says not to file it.
findings.quote: The stock photo on the login page — the woman laughing at a salad-adjacent laptop — is deeply corny.
findings.severity_reason: Purely cosmetic remark explicitly disclaimed as not a request by the customer.
findings.match_note: No catalogue analog; customer explicitly says 'Do not file Salad Susan,' confirming it should not become a ticket.
